purpose: Tigecycline is a strong antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including complicated skin infections, abdominal infections, and a type of pneumonia caught in the community. It is used when other antibiotics may not work well, often for infections caused by hard-to-treat bacteria. Your doctor will use it when the infection is serious enough to require treatment in a hospital.
how_it_works: Tigecycline works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to survive and grow. Think of it like cutting off the bacteria's food supply — without those proteins, the bacteria cannot multiply and your immune system can fight them off. It works against a wide range of bacteria, including some that have become resistant to other antibiotics.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. You may also experience stomach upset, headache, or dizziness. Some patients notice a temporary increase in certain liver enzyme levels on their blood tests.
warnings: Important: Studies have shown that tigecycline may carry a slightly higher risk of death compared to some other antibiotics, so it is only used when truly necessary and other options are not suitable. It should not be used during pregnancy as it can harm an unborn baby or affect bone and tooth development. Tell your doctor about all your medications and health conditions before starting this medicine. It is given as an IV infusion in the hospital, not taken by mouth.
typical_dosing: Tigecycline is given through an IV (a drip into your vein) in the hospital. The usual starting dose is 100 mg given once, followed by 50 mg every 12 hours (twice a day). Each dose is given slowly over about 30 to 60 minutes. Treatment typically lasts 5 to 14 days depending on the type and severity of your infection.
